rules: Any liquid asset: stock, crypto, or leveraged/inverse ETF
Rotate each 6:30am CT run — sell yesterday, buy today's best
Leverage matched to conviction; asymmetric payoff preferred
Hard stop at entry; spot-crypto-only on weekends

positions.catalyst: SUNDAY 9/13 -- US EQUITY MARKET CLOSED, SO SPOT CRYPTO ONLY BY MANDATE; NO LEVERAGED OR INVERSE WRAPPER IS TRADABLE TODAY. Feed verified LIVE twice before pricing: proxy pulls returned asOf 2026-09-13T10:40:35.663Z and 10:42:09.882Z, and across those ~95 seconds BTC-USD moved 76,733.64 -> 76,711.53, ETH-USD 2,479.31 -> 2,478.99 and SOL-USD 99.66 -> 99.63, while ORCL sat frozen at 150.28 on both pulls -- the identical stale equity print it carried yesterday, which is exactly the signature of a live crypto tape against a dead equity tape. Cross-checked against Robinhood real-time crypto marks in the same minute: BTC 76,742.48 (0.04% from proxy), ETH 2,479.72 (0.02%), SOL 99.660835 (exact to the cent). Two independent feeds agree. CLOSED ETH-USD AT 2,478.99 FOR -$220.17 (-2.11%). THE SIGNAL I BOUGHT INVERTED INSIDE 24 HOURS AND MY OWN RISK SECTION NAMED IT. Yesterday I wrote, in the first sentence of the risk block, that 'relative strength is the weakest category of signal I trade, and it is essentially all I have today,' and that 'ETH went up more than BTC yesterday, therefore it will go up more than BTC today' is single-observation momentum extrapolation in thin weekend books. That is precisely what failed. Measured against my own recorded 9/12 marks, the last 24 hours read: BTC -0.79%, LTC -1.02%, AVAX -1.63%, DOGE -1.77%, LINK -1.83%, ADA -1.93%, ETH -2.10%, XRP -2.19%, SOL -2.34%. The entire complex is red and the ordering is a clean beta ladder -- the higher the beta, the worse the loss, with BTC losing least and SOL most. Robinhood's midnight-CT-anchored changes say the same thing on a shorter clock: BTC -0.58%, LTC -0.36%, AVAX -1.08%, LINK -1.36%, DOGE -1.45%, ETH -1.59%, XRP -1.60%, SOL -2.01%. This is not a random weekend drift -- it is a textbook deleveraging tape, and the research description matches it exactly: bitcoin is being used as the primary source of liquidity while higher-beta assets such as ether come under disproportionate pressure as traders reduce exposure. I was long the disproportionate-pressure side of that. THE ETH/BTC RATIO TEST I SET FOR MYSELF YESTERDAY HAS FAILED. I entered noting the ratio at 0.03275 and wrote plainly that the 0.035 weekly level required to confirm genuine rotation had not been reclaimed -- that I was 'buying a trend that is still unconfirmed by its own stated test.' The ratio now computes to 2,478.99 / 76,711.53 = 0.03232, lower than at entry and moving away from confirmation, not toward it. I am treating that as the test resolving against me rather than as noise, and I am not re-entering the same trade a day later at a worse ratio. TODAY IS AGAIN A LOW-EDGE DAY AND THE HONEST READ IS THAT THE DRIFT IS NEGATIVE. My window is Sunday ~05:45 CT to Monday ~06:30 CT: the back half of the weekend, the Sunday-evening Asia reopen, and the Monday Asia/Europe session. It ends BEFORE the US cash open, so I do not capture Monday's US session at all. There is no scheduled catalyst anywhere inside it. Everything on the calendar lands outside: the Senate cloture vote on the CLARITY Act is confirmed for 2:15pm ET Tuesday 9/15 (60 votes needed; last run I logged the date as uncertain between Monday and Tuesday -- multiple sources now agree on Tuesday, so that ambiguity is resolved), and the FOMC decision is Wednesday 9/16-17 with a 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% priced at roughly 83% on Polymarket and 86.5% on broader implied measures after the hot 9/11 CPI (headline 3.4% y/y, core +0.3% m/m) and hawkish communication from Chair Warsh. So the choice today is purely which spot asset to hold overnight into a hawkish week with no event to trade, and my own rules say that on low-edge days I park in lower-vol spot.
positions.driver: LONG BITCOIN (BTC-USD) SPOT, 1X, UNLEVERED -- 100% of capital (0.133017 BTC) at 76,711.53, $10,203.94 deployed, stop 72,108.84 (-6%). THIS IS THE DEFENSIVE PICK AND I AM LABELLING IT AS ONE RATHER THAN DRESSING IT UP. BTC will not be the biggest mover in the next 24 hours; if the complex bounces, ETH and SOL bounce harder, and I will underperform them. I am choosing it anyway because the mandate's objective is explicitly 'highest risk/reward WITH the most downside protection,' with a standing instruction to 'park in lower-vol/spot' on low-edge days, and this is the third consecutive genuinely low-edge session -- two of them weekends. WHAT MAKES BTC THE PICK RATHER THAN MERELY THE SAFE ANSWER IS THAT TODAY THE DEFENSIVE CHOICE AND THE RELATIVE-STRENGTH CHOICE ARE THE SAME ASSET, WHICH IS RARE. Normally 'lowest volatility' and 'best momentum' point in opposite directions and I have to pick one. Today BTC is simultaneously the lowest-variance instrument in the tradable universe AND the single best 24-hour performer in it (-0.79% against -2.10% for ETH and -2.34% for SOL), because the flow driving the tape is a rotation INTO bitcoin as the liquidity sink and out of beta. I get to align with the direction of flow without paying for it in variance. That is the closest thing to an edge available on a Sunday. THE MECHANICAL FLOW ARGUMENT, WHICH IS THE ONE NON-MOMENTUM REASON I HAVE. Spot BTC ETF redemptions were decelerating hard into the weekend -- $282.7M on 9/10 collapsing to $13.29M on 9/11 -- suggesting the marginal institutional seller was already exhausting, and the ETF creation/redemption mechanism is mechanically shut for my entire window regardless. I explicitly rejected this argument yesterday as 'the absence of a negative, not the presence of an edge,' and I still think that is right in isolation. But it is worth more paired with a tape where BTC is actively receiving rotation than it was paired with a tape where BTC was flat and ETH was running. The facts changed; the weight I give the argument changes with them. CHOSEN OVER, WITH THE COMPARATIVE ARGUMENT STATED: (a) 100% CASH at 10,203.90 -- the genuine runner-up, and closer to right than on any day I have logged. There is no catalyst, the macro drift is hostile, and a book that must rotate daily is permitted to sit out. I rejected it because holding the deepest, lowest-beta crypto asset for one weekend session after the complex has ALREADY flushed ~2% of beta is not the same risk as buying into a rally, and because if I am wrong today it will be by a fraction of a percent rather than by the 9.88% ORCL number. But I want it on the record that the margin between BTC and cash today is thin, and if tomorrow is also catalyst-free I should seriously consider that a flat book is the correct expression of 'no edge' rather than a smaller position in the safest asset. (b) HOLDING ETH-USD -- rejected outright. The stated confirmation test (ETH/BTC reclaiming 0.035 weekly) failed and the ratio moved the wrong way to 0.03232. Re-upping a thesis whose own invalidation criterion just triggered, purely because I am already in it, is the definition of a sunk-cost hold. (c) SPOT SOL at 99.63 (-2.34% 24h, -2.01% since midnight) -- the worst performer on the board, the highest beta, the thinnest weekend book, and no catalyst. Buying the biggest loser in a deleveraging tape is a bounce trade, and I have no signal that says the deleveraging is finished. Rejected. (d) SPOT XRP at 1.3417 (-2.19%) -- the most direct CLARITY Act beneficiary, since the bill would hand the CFTC exclusive spot-market jurisdiction and settle the classification question. Rejected on both timing and probability: the cloture vote is Tuesday, two days past my exit, and Polymarket odds of the bill becoming law in 2026 have collapsed from 82% in February to about 16% as of 9/6, with three unresolved disputes still blocking it (ethics provisions touching the President's crypto income, DeFi developer liability under Section 604, and the stablecoin-yield provision that threatens Coinbase's USDC rewards revenue). Positioning Sunday for a Tuesday whip count that the market prices as likely to fail is not a 24-hour trade. (e) SPOT LTC at 53.625 -- the only asset that held up comparably to BTC (-1.02% 24h, -0.36% since midnight). Rejected because that resilience has no explanation behind it, the book is an order of magnitude thinner than BTC's, and 'second-best defensive asset with no story and worse liquidity' has no argument over 'best defensive asset with the deepest book.' (f) LINK 11.338 (-1.83%), DOGE 0.08348 (-1.77%), AVAX 7.321 (-1.63%), ADA 0.20467 (-1.93%) -- all pure beta, all red, no catalysts. Nothing to say for any of them today. (g) EVERY LEVERAGED OR INVERSE WRAPPER -- BITX, the 2X Solana and inverse-BTC funds, SOXL/SOXS, TQQQ/SQQQ, the single-stock 2x products -- unavailable, equity market closed. Worth stating explicitly: if today were a weekday, the deleveraging tape plus a hawkish FOMC two days out would make an INVERSE expression the obvious high-conviction trade, and I would be sizing one. The reason I am long a defensive asset instead of short a beta one is the calendar, not the analysis. That asymmetry -- being structurally unable to express the bearish view on weekends -- is a real limitation of this book and it has now cost me on two consecutive Saturdays-and-Sundays. ON THE STOP, WHERE I AM DEVIATING FROM THE PRIOR RUN'S READING OF THE RULE. The rule string is 's ~ 0.06 unleveraged / 0.08 for 2x / 0.10 for 3x-2xcrypto-spot,' which is ambiguous about where plain spot sits; yesterday's run read spot into the 0.10 bucket and set ETH at -10%. I am reading BTC spot as UNLEVERED and using 6%, for a substantive reason rather than a textual one: BTC's realized daily volatility is roughly half ETH's, so a 6% band on BTC is approximately the volatility-equivalent of the 10% band on ETH -- it sits a comparable number of daily standard deviations away. A 10% stop on an asset that moved 0.79% today would be a disaster marker, not a risk control. 72,108.84 is a level BTC only reaches on a genuine regime break.
positions.risks: THE PRIMARY RISK IS THAT I AM BUYING THE ASSET THAT JUST WON, ON A ONE-DAY LOOKBACK -- WHICH IS THE EXACT SIGNAL THAT COST ME MONEY YESTERDAY. I need to be blunt about this rather than let the direction of the trade disguise it. Yesterday I bought ETH because it had outperformed BTC over 24 hours. Today I am buying BTC because it has outperformed ETH over 24 hours. That is the same methodology producing the opposite answer, and if the complex mean-reverts tonight -- which is the single most common thing a beaten-down crypto tape does over a weekend -- I will have bought the low-beta asset one session before the high-beta bounce and underperformed twice in a row by whipsawing. The partial defence is that BTC's case does not rest only on momentum: it is independently the lowest-variance, deepest-liquidity asset in the mandated universe, so the momentum signal is pointing the same direction as the risk-control requirement rather than being the whole argument. But I would be lying if I said the 24-hour ladder was not what moved me off cash. A RELIEF BOUNCE IS THE MOST LIKELY WAY THIS UNDERPERFORMS, AND I AM POSITIONED AGAINST IT. The complex has flushed roughly 2% of beta in 24 hours with no news. Thin Sunday books that sell off on flow rather than information frequently retrace on Sunday evening when Asia reopens and the liquidation pressure lifts. In that scenario SOL and ETH recover 3-4% and BTC recovers 1%, and the correct trade today was the one I explicitly rejected in (c). I have no way to distinguish 'deleveraging has further to run' from 'deleveraging is done and this is the low' -- I am simply declining to guess, and declining to guess has a cost in a book whose purpose is asymmetric payoff. THE ASYMMETRY THIS BOOK EXISTS TO CAPTURE IS ESSENTIALLY ABSENT TODAY AND I AM NOT GOING TO PRETEND OTHERWISE. Spot BTC at 1x over a weekend session realistically produces a move of well under 1% in either direction -- today's own realized move was 0.79%. That is a near-flat outcome for a 100% all-in mandate, and it is the third straight session of low-variance positioning. Two of those three were forced by the calendar; this one is only partly forced, because SOL and XRP were available and would have been higher-variance. The honest framing is that I chose variance reduction over expected return on a day when I could not identify positive expected return anywhere, and if I am going to keep doing that, cash is the cleaner expression of it. THE MACRO IS A HEADWIND AND BTC IS NOT IMMUNE, ONLY LESS EXPOSED. A 25bp hike is roughly 83-86% priced for Wednesday and Chair Warsh has been communicating hawkishly into it. Crypto is a long-duration, zero-cashflow asset class and a rising real-yield path is a structural negative for all of it -- BTC included. I argued yesterday that this was 'largely pre-paid' and the market then found more room to reprice; I made the same argument about CPI on 9/11 and it was wrong then too. I am now making it for a third time, so I will state it as the weakness it is: my base case assumes a priced-in event cannot hurt me, and that assumption has been falsified twice in four sessions. What is different today is only that the event sits three days outside my window, not that the reasoning is better. WEEKEND MECHANICS AND THE STOP, STATED PLAINLY. 72,108.84 is a number in a JSON file, not a resting order -- the same limitation that let ORCL trade through 154.16 and cost me $1,142.56. Crypto trades continuously so there is no gap mechanism, but there is also no close: a 3am liquidation cascade is fully live against me with no one watching and no mechanism to exit. BTC is the deepest book in the asset class and will absorb weekend flow better than anything else available, which is a real mitigant, but it is a mitigant and not a guarantee. COUNTER-EVIDENCE I AM DISCOUNTING, STATED FAIRLY. The BTC ETF outflow streak is a multi-day pattern of institutional distribution and roughly -$1B net for 2026; the deceleration I am leaning on is two data points ($282.7M to $13.29M) and could simply be a Friday effect rather than exhaustion. ETH's structural case -- 42M+ ETH staked, exchange balances down ~15% since June, ETH ETFs leading 2026 net flows at about +$863M -- has not disappeared just because the ratio fell for one day; it is a months-timescale argument and one bad session does not refute it, which means my 'test failed' framing is itself slightly too tidy. And a Sunday-evening leak of a favourable CLARITY whip count would lift the whole complex with the high-beta names leading, leaving BTC the worst place to be. THE PROCESS LESSON, CARRIED FORWARD AND MADE SPECIFIC. On 9/11 I wrote that naming a risk is not managing it, and that when I identify THE risk inside my holding window it should change the position rather than just the paragraph. Yesterday I named single-observation relative strength as the weakest signal I trade and then traded it anyway at full size -- so the lesson was written down and not applied. Today's concrete application: I have set the stop by volatility-equivalence rather than by copying the prior run's band, I have stated cash as a live runner-up rather than a rhetorical one, and I have flagged in advance that a fourth consecutive catalyst-free day should produce a FLAT book, not another defensive asset. That is a pre-commitment the next run can hold me to. PRICING AND PROCEDURE. MITIGANTS: spot at 1x has no daily reset, no decay, no path dependency and no wrapper counterparty, so tomorrow's mark is a clean price; BTC is the deepest and least volatile instrument in the tradable universe and will be fully liquid at 06:30 CT Monday; there is no scheduled event inside the holding window; the position is aligned with the observable direction of rotation flow rather than against it; the 6% stop is volatility-calibrated rather than nominal; and the scheduler has now fired on time for a fifth consecutive session, so no multi-day carry distorts the mark.
